title: Character decomposition and eigenvector lifting for semilinear local actions
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a commutative local ring with residue field $k=A/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $H$ be a finite abelian group of order $N\ge1$, acting on $A$ by ring automorphisms, trivially on $k$. Suppose $N$ is a unit in $A$ and there is an $H$-fixed unit $\zeta\in A$ with $\zeta^N=1$ and $1-\zeta^a\in A^\times$ for $1\le a<N$. Let $M$ be an $A$-module with an additive $H$-action satisfying $h(am)=h(a)h(m)$, and let $L\subset M$ be an $H$-stable $A$-submodule with $\mathfrak mM\subseteq L$. Assume $V=M/L$ is finite-dimensional over $k$. For a group homomorphism $\chi:H\to\langle\zeta\rangle\subset A^\times$, write $V_\chi=\{v:h(v)=\overline{\chi(h)}v\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. Then $V=\bigoplus_\chi V_\chi$. Any linearly independent list of nonzero vectors each spanning an $H$-stable line can be extended to an eigenvector basis of $V$. The additive map
$$e_\chi(m)=N^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}\chi(h)^{-1}h(m)$$
satisfies $h(e_\chi(m))=\chi(h)e_\chi(m)$. If the class of $m$ lies in $V_\chi$, $e_\chi(m)$ has the same class as $m$. Moreover $e_\chi$ preserves every $H$-stable $A$-submodule of $M$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.5, proof: diagonalization of the cotangent representation and character averaging, printed p.124. The statement isolates the semilinear algebra used there.

proof.text: Write $q:M\to V$ for the quotient map. Since $L$ is stable, $h(q(m))=q(h(m))$ is well-defined. For $a\in A$, semilinearity gives $h(\bar a q(m))=\overline{h(a)}q(h(m))=\bar a h(q(m))$, because $H$ acts trivially on $k$; changing $a$ by an element of $\mathfrak m$ has no effect since $\mathfrak mM\subseteq L$. Thus the quotient action is $k$-linear. Put $C=\langle\zeta\rangle\subset A^\times$. Its elements are $1,\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^{N-1}$: these are distinct because $1-\zeta^a$ is a unit for $0<a<N$. Reduction $\iota:C\to k^\times$ is injective for the same reason: equality of two reductions would put the unit $1-\zeta^a$ in $\mathfrak m$. Hence $C$ is cyclic of order $N$, and distinct characters $H\to C$ remain distinct after reduction. Finally $\bar N\ne0$, since $N$ is a unit.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.5, proof, printed p.124; detailed semilinear-algebra expansion by Q31.

proof.text: Every $g\in H$ fixes $N^{-1}$ and $\chi(h)$, because ring automorphisms fix integers and their unit inverses and $\chi(h)$ is a power of the fixed unit $\zeta$. Additivity, semilinearity and the bijection $h\mapsto t=gh$ give $$g(e_\chi(m))=N^{-1}\sum_h\chi(h)^{-1}(gh)(m)=N^{-1}\sum_t\chi(g^{-1}t)^{-1}t(m)=\chi(g)e_\chi(m).$$ The map $e_\chi$ is additive. If $P\subset M$ is any stable $A$-submodule and $m\in P$, every summand $\chi(h)^{-1}h(m)$ is in $P$, so $e_\chi(m)\in P$. In particular $L$ is preserved and $e_\chi$ induces $p_\chi:V\to V$, $p_\chi(v)=\bar N^{-1}\sum_h\iota(\chi(h))^{-1}h(v)$. This is $k$-linear by step 1 and its image lies in $V_\chi$ by the displayed identity.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.5, proof, printed p.124; detailed semilinear-algebra expansion by Q31.

proof.text: If $q(m)=v\in V_\chi$, then $$q(e_\chi(m))=p_\chi(v)=\bar N^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}\iota(\chi(h))^{-1}\iota(\chi(h))v=\bar N^{-1}\bar N v=v.$$ This proves the lifting assertion and also $p_\chi|_{V_\chi}=\mathrm{id}$, with no assumption that the original action on $M$ is $A$-linear.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.5, proof, printed p.124; detailed semilinear-algebra expansion by Q31.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-finite-character-fourier-kernel] to the field $k$, the groups $H,C$ and the injection $\iota$ from step 1; the order and nonvanishing hypotheses were verified there. Interchanging the two finite sums gives, for every $v\in V$, $$\sum_{\chi:H\to C}p_\chi(v)=\bar N^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}\left(\sum_\chi\iota(\chi(h))^{-1}\right)h(v)=v.$$ Each summand belongs to $V_\chi$ by step 2, so these eigenspaces span $V$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.5, proof, printed p.124; detailed semilinear-algebra expansion by Q31.

proof.text:
For $v\in V_\psi$, the formula for $p_\chi$ shows that $p_\chi(v)$ is a scalar multiple of $v$, and hence lies in both $V_\psi$ and $V_\chi$. If $\chi
e\psi$, choose $g$ with $\iota(\chi(g))
e\iota(\psi(g))$ by step 1. A vector $w$ in the intersection satisfies $(\iota(\chi(g))-\iota(\psi(g)))w=0$, so $w=0$ over the field $k$. Thus $p_\chi(v)=0$ for $\chi
e\psi$, while step 3 gives $p_\chi(v)=v$ for $\chi=\psi$. Applying $p_\chi$ to any finite relation $\sum_\psi v_\psi=0$ isolates $v_\chi=0$. Together with step 4 this is exactly $V= igoplus_\chi V_\chi$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.5, proof, printed p.124; detailed semilinear-algebra expansion by Q31.

proof.text: Let $v\ne0$ span a stable line $D=kv\subset V$. The explicit formula for $p_\chi$ is a linear combination of the operators $h$, so $p_\chi(D)\subseteq D$. Since $v=\sum_\chi p_\chi(v)$ by step 4, some $p_\chi(v)$ is nonzero. It is both a scalar multiple of $v$ and a vector of $V_\chi$, so $v\in V_\chi$. Step 5 makes this character unique. Therefore every vector in the prescribed independent list is already an eigenvector for one of the indexed characters.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.5, proof, printed p.124; detailed semilinear-algebra expansion by Q31.

proof.text: Partition the prescribed independent list according to its unique character from step 6. For each $\chi$, this gives an independent subset of the vector space $V_\chi$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector] to extend that subset to a basis $B_\chi$ of $V_\chi$ (including the empty subset and the zero space). The union of the $B_\chi$ spans $V$ by step 4. Any finite relation in that union separates into relations in the individual $V_\chi$ by step 5, and each relation is zero by independence of $B_\chi$. Thus the union is an eigenvector basis containing every prescribed vector. Since $V$ is finite-dimensional, retain the prescribed order and list the remaining finitely many basis vectors afterward.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q31-8ad89e0a1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node lem-per-finite-character-fourier-kernel, the cited node lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector and ILO VIII 5.3.4–5.3.6 (printed pp.123–125). The item's statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the base, checked against the Q105 run snapshot. All seven steps are correct. (1) The quotient action is k-linear, the powers of ζ are distinct and reduce injectively, and N is nonzero in k. (2) The substitution t=gh gives h(e_χ(m))=χ(h)e_χ(m), and e_χ preserves stable submodules term by term. (3) e_χ fixes the class of an eigenvector. (4) The new node gives Σ_χ p_χ = id. (5) The V_χ intersect trivially and the projectors isolate the components of a relation, so V is their direct sum. (6) A vector spanning a stable line is an eigenvector. (7) Basis extension inside each V_χ gives an eigenbasis containing the prescribed list. This is the diagonalization ILO 5.3.5 leaves out, now written in full, and it matches what the citer's step 4 uses. The new node is true: Hom(H,C) has N elements and separates points, and reindexing by a character with ψ(h)≠1 kills the sum. I tested it on the trivial group, ℤ/2 over 𝔽_3, (ℤ/2)² with ℤ/4 in 𝔽_5 and ℤ/4 over 𝔽_5. It is not a restatement of the item, not a duplicate (the closest nodes are fd-character-orthogonality, per-finite-character-annihilator-duality and sfb-character-eigenspaces-independent), and not a one-line Mathlib leaf. The node's form is right: statement only, own objects, recorded searches, correct blueprint fields. There is no SGA citation and no repair note. Note for the maintainer: the item's via chain runs through the dropped 2026-10-19 Gabber purity branch, which is a reachability question, not a fault of this split. No fixes.
